100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 14, 1926, the U.S. Senate voted to approve the McNary-Haugen Bill, aimed at providing price supports for farmers, a move that could reshape American agriculture. In Europe, tensions escalated as the League of Nations grappled with ongoing disputes over territories in the aftermath of World War I. Meanwhile, in the world of entertainment, the silent film "The Son of the Sheik," featuring Rudolph Valentino, captivated audiences, marking a significant moment in the transition to talkies.
